Sauyo Quezon City Dear Ms. Bayona: This has reference to your letter dated January 28, 2025, requesting this Department's opinion on the Implementation of the demolition by Copriss of Quezon City by virtue ot a) Section 2 (c) of Quezon City Ordinance No. SP-2444 S-2015; and b) Ordinance No. 2807, Series of 2019 dated February 22, 2019. In your letter, you informed this Department of the following salient facts and circumstances: 1. 2. 3. 4. Sometime in 1985, you settled in an unoccupied parcel of land allegedly owned by the "Carlos Family" in Barangay Sauyo, Quezon City; That, you have been in peaceful possession of the land until 2010, when other group of settlers entered the area alleging ownership of the land, and even formed their Association. Ordinance No. sp 2444 " AN ORDINANCE DISQUALIFYING AS BENEFICIARIES FROM THE SOCIALIZED HOUSING PROGRAM OF THE CITY GOVERNMENT OR ANY NATIONAL AGENCY THOSE WHO COMMIT ACTS OF UNJUSTIFIED AND DELIBERATE REFUSAL OF NON-CONFORMITST OCCUPANTS AND/OR RECALCITRANTS TO BE COVERED BY THE SAID PR"GRAM" and; Ordinance No. sp 2807 " AN ORDINANCE APPROVING THE SUBDIVISION PLAN OF VILLA ROSARIO HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC. WITH TWO HUNDRED TWENTY-TWO (222) SALEABLE LOTS UNDER COMMUNITY MORTGAGE PROGRAM (CMP) LOCATED AT LOT 2, (LRC) PCS-2104, SAUYO ROAD (NAVAL EXTENTION) BARANGAY SAUYO, QUEZON CITY, METRO MANILA, REGISTERED IN THE NAME OF ROSARIO L. SORIANO, COVERED BY TRANSFER CERTIFICATE OF TITLE NUMBERED RF07571 OF THE REGISTRY OF DEEDS OF QUEZON CITY, CONTAINING AN AREA OF TEN THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED THREE (10,803.00) SQUARE METERES AS APPLIED FOR BY ITS HOA PRESIDENT EMERLINDA D. PURSUANT TO SECTION 9, RULE Ill OF THE IMPLEMENTING STANDARDS, RULES AND REGULATIONS OF BP BLDG 220" were enacted by the City Government of Quezon; 5. As the influx of settlers continued, individuals undertook various improvements to the land prompting brokers and leaders to assert their rights through the enforcement of the aforementioned Ordinance; 6. On January 22, 2025, COPRISS started harassing and even sent out letters demanding you to settle payments if there is no showing of any agreements or approved subdivision plans; 7. That, until this day you believed that the Ordinance, COPRISS and the Demolition Order has no legal basis in fact and in law; At the outset, this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it has no authority to declare invalid any ordinance or resolution of the local Sanggunian, or any acts committed by the members thereof which alleged to be in violation of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 or other applicable laws. Moreover, Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated September 17, 2010 provides that the Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: l. Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better rights over a given controversy; 2. Those presumptively valid acts, e.g. enacted ordinances. consummated acts that already enioy the presumption of reqularity on the part of the public officer concerned. and similar instances: 3. Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself request for the opinion. In the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective; and those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government. Since the questioned ordinance was passed in 2015 and 2019, respectively. This Department is of the position that the same is effective and valid. Thus, only the competent court has the authority to decide on the validity of an ordinance upon initiation of appropriate action such as a petition for declaration of nullity of the resolution or ordinance.lln this regard, considering that the matter at hand is justiciable in nature as it may ripen into a full-blown litigation, we are proscribed from issuing our opinion. With respect to your query on the demolition by COPRISS, it is beyond the province of this Department to issue any injunction or to stay the execution of any demolition, as such matter falls within the purview of the court. Further, we highly encourage you to sought the assistance of the Department of Human Settlement and Urban Development DILG Legal opinion NO. 20. series of 2016, June 23, 2016. Page 2 of3

(DHSUD) for any concerns pertaining to your issue, as they are the competent authority to address such matter effectively. Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same, We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LLRALD/mag Page 3 or 3
